alt: Looping animation of a hexagonal spiral lattice in orange and violet, two cells across, with a white mirror line through γ and white symbols marking the centres α, β and γ of its symmetry.
caption: The published animation: one period of 6.390159918584649 time units in 48 frames, two cells across. Drawn on it are two motions that generate its symmetry r3₂∗3: the mirror μ through γ, which costs nothing, since every frame is symmetric across it, and an anticlockwise third of a turn about β, which gives the film two thirds of a period later. At β, as at every centre between the mirrors, the chemicals barely move; the film turns around them.

alt: Stroboscopic animation, one frame per period. It begins as a sharp spiral lattice, slowly loses contrast over the first third, and ends as an almost flat field blinking in unison.
caption: Why you cannot simply simulate. This starts exactly on the published orbit, disturbed only by single-precision round-off, and simulates forward with the three zero-cost symmetries imposed at every step. One frame per period, 313 periods: the spirals fade, by period 135 none are left, and every point ends up oscillating in unison.
